title: Investment Statement

origin.title: Sample Fidelity Portfolio Account Statement
origin.clearance_note: Fidelity's own sample statement, published on fidelity.com to show customers what a monthly statement looks like. Every page is marked '*** SAMPLE STATEMENT *** For informational purposes only'. All personal data is specimen: the account holder is 'John W. Doe, 100 Main St.', the account numbers are 111-111111, 222-222222 and 333-333333, and the phone numbers are Fidelity's and SIPC's published lines. No redaction needed.

notes: Features one complete row of the page 7 stock holdings table: the ENSTAR GROUP short position. It is the hardest row on the page: a negative quantity (-100.00) and market value (-13,710.00), a cost basis carrying a superscript footnote marker (-14,510.99c), a positive unrealized gain despite the negative values, and a description that wraps onto a second line holding the ticker. The row reconciles: -13,710.00 - (-14,510.99) = 800.99. Page 1's portfolio reconciliation was the first choice and grounds perfectly, but a clean summary table is the easy case. Price is extracted but not featured, to keep to five fields. The first account's beginning value extracts as 880853.95 because Fidelity's PDF prints '$88,0853.95', a typo in the sample; the column arithmetic and page 4 give 88,053.95. preview_pages shows the summary, an account summary with its allocation chart, the featured holdings page and the estimated cash flow table, instead of the default pick, which included a page of footnotes.
